title: In this town, your reflection does what you really want to do
premise: In a town where every reflection does what its owner really wants, the narrator has no reflection at all and takes it to mean he wants nothing. His fiancee Remi is getting their beach hut ready for summer while he stays in the doorway on his laptop, and her reflection in the hut window walks a little further down the shore each day.
twist: Remi's reflection was following his. His own reflection was never missing: what he really wants is to walk the shore with her, so it had been out there doing it all along, where he never looked. The rule that seemed to show she wanted to leave means they both wanted the same walk.
world: a row of twelve faded pastel beach huts on a windy off-season shore, glossy wet sand that mirrors, a breakwater and a bench at the point, and a second deckchair that is set out every morning
